prompt: Why didn't Harvard have calculus classes when it first opened?
answer:
Harvard didn’t offer calculus when it opened in 1636 because calculus had not yet been developed as a formal mathematical discipline. Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz created its foundations independently several decades later, in the late 17th century.

Harvard’s early curriculum instead emphasized classical subjects such as Latin, Greek, theology, logic, arithmetic, and geometry. Calculus was introduced at Harvard only later, during the 18th century, as the new methods and textbooks spread from Europe.
